findings.title: One SendGrid failure aborts every remaining cancellation and skips all DB deletes
findings.body:
A single try/catch wraps the whole `for` loop over `remindersToCancel`. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder (transient error, the 100-cancellation cap, or a batch that already has a cancel status), the loop exits. No later reminders in that run are cancelled, so their emails go out.

The deletes are also lost. They are collected as lazy `PrismaPromise`s and only run at `Promise.all` after the loop, so none of them execute when the catch fires, including deletes for reminders that SendGrid did cancel. On the next run those reminders are retried. Re-cancelling an already-cancelled batch fails again, so the same reminder can block the whole loop every 15 minutes until its date passes.

There is a concrete trigger. `requestReschedule` flags a reminder `cancelled: true`. `handleNewBooking` then cancels the same batch immediately on reschedule but leaves the row. The cron later re-POSTs that batch.

Fix: wrap each reminder in its own try/catch and run (await) its delete right after its own cancel succeeds.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation misses bookings cancelled shortly before the reminder fires
findings.body:
Cancellation now only happens in the cron, which runs every 15 minutes. Each run first deletes all EMAIL reminders whose `scheduledDate <= now`, and only then cancels flagged reminders.

If a booking is cancelled or rescheduled after the last cron run but before the reminder's send time, the next run deletes the row without ever calling SendGrid's cancel. The email is sent. Example: cron runs at :45, reminder at :50, booking cancelled at :46.

Even when the cron does catch it, it may only be a few minutes before the send. SendGrid does not guarantee cancellations made less than about 10 minutes before the send time.

The old code cancelled immediately, so this is a regression for late cancellations. `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` should cancel right away when `scheduledDate` is near (e.g. within the next hour + cron interval), and only defer far-future reminders.

findings.title: Reschedule path still cancels in SendGrid immediately, reintroducing the pending-cancellation cap
findings.body:
The PR says cancelled and rescheduled bookings are deferred to the cron to stay under SendGrid's limit of 100 pending cancellations. Here, though, every reschedule calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., true)`. That POSTs a cancel to `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` right away for reminders that may be up to 72h out.

Reschedules are common, so these still pile up in `scheduled_sends` and can hit the cap. Once the cap is reached the call fails, the error is only logged, and the email is still sent.

This path also re-cancels reminders that `requestReschedule` already flagged `cancelled: true`, which leads to the duplicate cancel described for the cron. Use the deferred (flag) path here, as `bookings.tsx` and `handleCancelBooking` do.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels in SendGrid but leaves the DB row in an inconsistent state
findings.body:
With `immediateDelete`, the function POSTs the cancel and returns. It neither deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row nor updates it.

For workflow or step deletion the row is cascade-deleted afterwards, so that case is fine. In the reschedule path, the original booking's rows stay with `scheduled: true` and a valid `referenceId`.

- If the row was already flagged `cancelled: true` (e.g. by `requestReschedule`), the cron will try to cancel the same batch again. That can fail and abort the cron loop.
- If the immediate POST fails (e.g. the cancellation cap), nothing records the failure and nothing retries, so the email is sent.

Fix: after a successful immediate cancel, delete the row. On failure, set `cancelled: true` so the cron retries.

findings.title: Reminder cancellation is fire-and-forget; the try/catch around it in handleNewBooking does nothing
findings.body:
The only thing that now stops a cancelled booking's email is the `cancelled: true` DB update (or the delete/SMS cancel). These calls are no longer awaited:

- `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` / `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` here
- the same calls in `bookings.tsx` `requestReschedule` (line 490)
- the same calls in `handleNewBooking`

Before this PR, the DB deletes were awaited via `Promise.all`. Now the handler can respond before the flag is written. Under serverless execution the update can be dropped, and any failure is only logged.

In `handleNewBooking` (lines 965-975), the surrounding try/catch is ineffective because the async calls are never awaited.

Fix: collect the promises and `await Promise.all(...)` before returning.
